Stress-test a proposed v2 plan for the ev-auto-trader-canada Next.js project at `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/`. Read-only — do not edit anything except suggesting plan changes back to me in your response.

**Context:**
Ian is buying a Hyundai or Kia EV in Canada within 1-2 weeks. Cash buyer, Ontario primary, no trade-in. He's running this as a personal-use deal-tracker, not a product. The repo has been live on Vercel for ~3 weeks. The previous session shipped tasks A, B, C, J, K, L from `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/NEXT.md`. Five blockers documented in `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/BLOCKERS_MEDIUM.md`.

**Read these files first** (full read, no skimming):
- `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/NEXT.md`
- `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/BLOCKERS_MEDIUM.md`
- `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/PROGRESS.md`
- `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/scripts/build_units_from_at.py`
- `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/scripts/enrich_units_from_listings.py`
- `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/scripts/snapshot.mjs`
- `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/src/lib/scoring.ts`
- `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/src/lib/types.ts`
- `/Users/ianmcadam/ev-auto-trader-canada/data/snapshots/` — list contents
- One snapshot JSON (any one) to understand schema

**My proposed v2 plan (4 phases). Critique it.**

### Phase 1 — Data integrity (highest priority, no external dependencies)

1.1 **Snapshot-derived daysOnLot**: Add `scripts/compute_days_on_lot.py` that walks `data/snapshots/*.json` (currently 3 snapshots: 2025-04-01, 2025-04-15, 2026-05-01), finds earliest snapshot containing each unit_id, computes (today - earliestDate) in days, writes `data/days-on-lot.json` keyed by unit_id. Then extend `loadUnits()` enrichment merge in `src/lib/data.ts` to overlay this if `daysOnLot` is null. Unblocks BLOCKERS_MEDIUM #5 + NEXT task E without any scraping.

1.2 **MSRP source discriminator**: Add `msrpSource: "scraped" | "default" | "spec-lookup" | "configurator"` to `InventoryUnit` schema in `src/lib/types.ts`. Update `scripts/build_units_from_at.py` to track which source provided the MSRP. UI renders different chip per source. Replaces the heuristic `ask > msrp + 5000` warning.

1.3 **Trim parser hardening**: In `scripts/build_units_from_at.py` `match_trim()`, add Ioniq5 "Ultimate Package" detection (currently maps to Preferred Long Range, real MSRP is ~$67k not $55k). Add Ioniq9 Calligraphy/Performance hierarchy. Add EV9 GT-Line detection. Build per-model trim-token tables instead of generic AWD-only fallbacks.

1.4 **EV9 spec lookup gap fix**: 18 EV9 units exist but all fall through to DEFAULT_MSRP. Investigate: are units MY2024 while specs only have MY2025? Either backfill MY2024 EV9 specs or relax `msrp_lookup` key to match on (model, trim) when year doesn't align.

### Phase 2 — Data acquisition unblock (Imperva workaround)

2.1 **Investigate AutoTrader search-results JSON endpoint**: The per-listing `/cars/` and `/offers/` HTML pages get blocked at request 7. But the search-results page itself may return JSON via an internal API call. If yes: scrape that, get daysOnMarket + dealer phone in bulk per request, no per-listing fetches needed. This is the killer fix for blockers 1 + 2 + 5 + task H.

2.2 **Apify fallback decision**: If 2.1 doesn't work, present user with cost/value of Apify AutoTrader actor (~$10/run for ~5k listings, ~$50/month if run weekly). User decides spend before any integration code.

2.3 **Imperva-evasion improvements** (only if 2.1 + 2.2 both fail): Rotate UA per request, add accept-language jitter, install `cloudscraper` Python package, randomize cadence between 3-8 seconds.

### Phase 3 — Decision-support features (negotiation toolkit)

3.1 **Per-unit negotiation card**: In `src/components/UnitDrawer.tsx`, add a section that renders: "Compared to the lowest comparable nationwide (model, trim, year): $X delta. Dealer has Y same-trim units, average Z days on lot. Used market retention W%. Suggested offer: $V (P% below ask)." All numbers come from existing computed data (used-market stats, dealer pressure map, snapshot-derived days).

3.2 **Email script generator**: Copy-button in UnitDrawer that emits a templated email to the dealer using the negotiation card data. Plain text, no markup. Customizable greeting via cookie.

3.3 **Cross-province delivery breakdown**: Currently transport is a flat per-province band. Add per-dealer breakdown: "Best deal in {province} for this trim is $X. After ${transport} transport, your effective OTD is $Y, saving ${delta} vs Ontario dealer." Renders inline in InventoryTable detail row when buyerProvince=ON.

### Phase 4 — Polish + ritual + commit

4.1 **Heat-pump trim flags** (NEXT task D): Schema extension in `src/lib/types.ts` for `Spec.heatPump: boolean | null`. Ian hand-fills from hyundai.ca/kia.ca trim sheets (5 min per nameplate). Defer if Phases 1-3 run over.

4.2 **Daily snapshot ritual + commit cadence**: Snapshot already runs via `npm run snapshot`. Make it part of the deploy ritual.

4.3 **Final commits + push**: 89d3cd5 + uncommitted Top Deals filter + MSRP chip + BLOCKERS_MEDIUM.md + Phase 1-3 work.

---

**Your task:**

For each of the 4 phases, give:

1. **Validation**: Is this the right ordering? Is anything actually blocking another item that I missed? 
2. **Risks I haven't considered**: Each phase, what's the highest-likelihood failure mode?
3. **Time estimate**: in tokens (chat-turns), not hours. Be concrete: how many file edits, how many subagent dispatches, how many user-decision pauses?
4. **Pruning candidates**: What in this plan is over-engineered for a 1-2 week purchase decision?
5. **Missing items from NEXT.md or BLOCKERS_MEDIUM.md**: Anything I'm forgetting?
6. **Creative additions**: One concrete idea I haven't considered that would meaningfully accelerate Ian's buy decision.

Hard constraint: this plan must be EXECUTABLE in a way that splits cleanly between (high-reasoning architectural work) and (medium-reasoning mechanical work). Tag each task with its required reasoning level: HIGH or MEDIUM.

Be skeptical. If a phase is wrong, say so explicitly. If a creative addition would 10x the value, name it clearly. If something will eat 80% of the budget for 20% of the value, kill it.

Caveman style fine. Bullets over prose. No padding.

10	## 1. AutoTrader Imperva blocked enrichment after 6-8 fetches
11	
12	**Where:** `scripts/enrich_units_from_listings.py`
13	**Symptom:** First 6 fetches returned 300 KB+ HTML and parsed VIN +
14	phone + streetAddress cleanly. Imperva then began returning 953-byte
15	challenge pages, then HTTP 403. `data/units-enrichment.json` ended up
16	with 8 entries instead of the expected 97.
17	**Root cause hypothesis:** Static UA string + raw `urllib` predictable
18	fingerprint + sub-3-second cadence = soft block at request 7.
19	**Fix candidates (high-reasoning):**
20	- Rotate user-agent + accept-language headers per request.
21	- Drop in `cloudscraper` or `curl_cffi` (ja3 fingerprinting).
22	- Use Apify AutoTrader actor (already loaded as MCP) with paid credits.
23	- Switch to scraping the AutoTrader **search-results** JSON endpoint
24	  rather than per-listing HTML — search responses include `daysOnMarket`
25	  + dealerPhone in one payload.
26	**Money required?** Apify ~$10/run for ~5k listings. User must approve.
27	**Workaround in place:** UI handles missing daysOnLot gracefully ("—");
28	$/km column treats missing range as "—"; dealer phone enrichment merge
29	runs over whatever is in the file.
30	
31	## 2. `/offers/` listing pages don't expose daysOnLot or MSRP
32	
33	**Where:** `scripts/enrich_units_from_listings.py` PATTERNS map
34	**Symptom:** Even on the 8 successful fetches, `daysOnLot` and `msrp`
35	regex matched **zero times**. Inspection of one fetched page (335 KB)
36	showed no `daysRelative`, `firstListed`, `publishDate`, `MSRP` (other
37	than translation strings), or any "X days ago" rendered text.
38	**Root cause:** AutoTrader's `/offers/` URL family is for
39	**dealer-curated promotional listings**. Different DOM than regular
40	`/cars/` listings. The fields we want only render on the latter.
41	**Fix candidates (high-reasoning):**
42	- Pivot scrape source: AutoTrader public `/cars/` listings via the
43	  search-results JSON endpoint (per-listing HTML not needed).
44	- Or accept that days-on-lot is unknowable without per-dealer
45	  inventory feeds + use lastSeen tenure as a proxy.
46	**Workaround in place:** dealScore weights still functional but the
47	`daysOnLot` term contributes 0 for all 97 units → effectively a
48	3-component score (price 35%, incentive 30%, pressure 20% renormalized).
49	Acceptable for personal use; not great as a deal signal.
50	
51	## 3. 65/97 units show ask > MSRP — trim mismatch + stale defaults
52	
53	**Where:** `scripts/build_units_from_at.py` `DEFAULT_MSRP` table +
54	`match_trim()` parser.
55	**Symptom:** Worst examples (verified):
56	- 5× Ioniq9 Preferred Long Range RWD at ask $82-87k vs MSRP $64,999
57	  (delta +$18-22k).
58	- Most likely: real trims are Performance Calligraphy AWD ($79,999) or
59	  Calligraphy AWD with options + dealer markup. Parser collapses
60	  anything without explicit "AWD" + "Calligraphy" tokens to the cheapest
61	  Preferred RWD trim.
62	**Root cause:** `match_trim()` token-scoring + Ioniq9 fallback
63	(`if "AWD" in t: return AWD trim, else RWD`) is too crude for trim
64	hierarchies with shared base names. AND `DEFAULT_MSRP` table reflects
65	2024-early-2025 pricing — needs refresh against Hyundai.ca / Kia.ca
66	configurators.
67	**Mitigation shipped (this commit):**
68	- UI chip "MSRP unverified" when ask > msrp + $5k (InventoryTable).
69	- Top Deals on home page filters out same — no more poisoned best-deal
70	  table.
71	**Fix candidates (high-reasoning, ~45 min):**
72	- Spot-check 5 trims via Hyundai/Kia Canada configurators; refresh
73	  `DEFAULT_MSRP` table.
74	- Tighten `match_trim()` for Ioniq9 specifically: detect "Calligraphy",
75	  "Performance", "Long Range" tokens explicitly, build full trim string.
76	- Mark each unit's `msrp` source in data ("scraped" | "default" |
77	  "spec-lookup") so the UI can render confidence.
78	
79	## 4. Item L (VERIFY-trim regex improvement) is moot
80	
81	Already cleaned up in prior session. `grep -n VERIFY data/units.json`
82	returns nothing. Script's `match_trim()` fallback at line 105 still
83	returns `VERIFY: <title>` strings on parser failure but no current
84	units have one. Removing the dead branch is cosmetic — leave it as a
85	sentinel for future scrape-input pathologies.
86	
87	## 5. Score reweighting (NEXT.md item E) needs real daysOnLot data
88	
89	Cannot meaningfully reweight while daysOnLot is universally missing
90	(blocker #2). Defer until pagination + non-`/offers/` scrape ships.
91

95	
96	- Dealer enrichment merge in `loadDealers()` — 8 dealers now show
97	  real phone + street address from the partial enrichment.
98	- $/km of range column with sort + tooltip (renders "—" when spec
99	  missing — graceful degradation).
100	- "MSRP unverified" warning chip on InventoryTable rows.
101	- Top Deals home-page filter blocks ask > msrp + 5k contamination.
102

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Enrich units.json by visiting each listingUrl and parsing detail pages.
3	
4	Workflow proposed by user: high-reasoning ripped the listing index URLs into
5	units.json. This script (designed to run on medium reasoning) walks each URL
6	and pulls the fields the index pages don't expose:
7	
8	  - daysOnLot (AutoTrader shows "X days ago" near the listing date)
9	  - actual MSRP from the listing's price-breakdown widget (when present)
10	  - dealer phone number (footer / contact card)
11	  - dealer street address (contact card)
12	  - exterior + interior color (sometimes more accurate than URL slug)
13	  - VIN (when not blocked behind a contact form)
14	
15	Output: data/units-enrichment.json with one row per unit id. data.ts will be
16	updated to merge this on top of units.json so re-runs only touch the
17	enrichment file (units.json stays the canonical scrape).
18	
19	Run:    python3 scripts/enrich_units_from_listings.py [--limit N] [--ids id1,id2]
20	
21	Notes:
22	  - AutoTrader uses Imperva/Incapsula bot protection. WebFetch (per-URL
23	    fetches via Claude / a paid proxy) gets through; raw curl does not.
24	  - Designed to be resumable — already-enriched ids are skipped unless
25	    --force is passed.
26	  - Be polite: 2-3 sec sleep between fetches. ~80 dealers * ~1.2 listings
27	    each = ~100 fetches = ~5 minutes wall time.
28	"""
29	import argparse
30	import json
31	import re
32	import sys
33	import time
34	from pathlib import Path
35	from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
36	from urllib.error import URLError, HTTPError
37	
38	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
39	UNITS = ROOT / "data" / "units.json"
40	ENRICH = ROOT / "data" / "units-enrichment.json"
41	
42	UA = (
43	    "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 14_5) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 "
44	    "(KHTML, like Gecko) Version/17.5 Safari/605.1.15"
45	)
46	
47	# Regex map keyed by enrichment field. Each tuple is (compiled_pattern,
48	# group_index). Tuned against AutoTrader's Apr-2026 markup; revisit if the
49	# detail-page DOM changes.
50	PATTERNS = {
51	    "daysOnLot": re.compile(r"(\d+)\s+days?\s+(?:ago|on\s+lot)", re.I),
52	    "vin": re.compile(r'"vin"\s*:\s*"([A-HJ-NPR-Z0-9]{17})"'),
53	    "phone": re.compile(r'"telephone"\s*:\s*"([\+\d\(\)\-\.\s]{7,20})"'),
54	    "streetAddress": re.compile(r'"streetAddress"\s*:\s*"([^"]{3,80})"'),
55	    "msrp": re.compile(r'(?:MSRP|Manufacturer.{1,5}Suggested)[^\d]{0,40}\$?\s*([\d,]+)', re.I),
56	    "exteriorColor": re.compile(r'"exteriorColor"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"'),
57	    "interiorColor": re.compile(r'"interiorColor"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"'),
58	}
59	
60	
61	def fetch(url: str, timeout: int = 25) -> str | None:
62	    try:
63	        req = Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA, "Accept": "text/html"})
64	        with urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
65	            body = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
66	            # Imperva challenge bodies are tiny — skip.
67	            if len(body) < 5000:
68	                print(f"  bot-blocked ({len(body)} bytes)", file=sys.stderr)
69	                return None
70	            return body
71	    except (URLError, HTTPError) as e:
72	        print(f"  fetch error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
73	        return None
74	
75	
76	def parse(body: str) -> dict:
77	    out = {}
78	    for field, pat in PATTERNS.items():
79	        m = pat.search(body)
80	        if not m:
81	            continue
82	        val = m.group(1).strip()
83	        if field in ("daysOnLot", "msrp"):
84	            try:
85	                out[field] = int(val.replace(",", ""))
86	            except ValueError:
87	                pass
88	        else:
89	            out[field] = val
90	    return out
91	
92	
93	def main():
94	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
95	    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, help="enrich at most N units")
96	    ap.add_argument("--ids", help="comma-separated unit ids to (re-)enrich")
97	    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="re-fetch already-enriched units")
98	    ap.add_argument("--sleep", type=float, default=2.5, help="seconds between fetches")
99	    args = ap.parse_args()
100	
101	    units = json.loads(UNITS.read_text())
102	    enriched = json.loads(ENRICH.read_text()) if ENRICH.exists() else {}
103	
104	    target_ids = set(args.ids.split(",")) if args.ids else None
105	
106	    candidates = []
107	    for u in units:
108	        if not u.get("listingUrl"):
109	            continue
110	        if target_ids and u["id"] not in target_ids:
111	            continue
112	        if not args.force and u["id"] in enriched:
113	            continue
114	        candidates.append(u)
115	    if args.limit:
116	        candidates = candidates[: args.limit]
117	
118	    print(f"enriching {len(candidates)} units (skipping {len(enriched)} already done)")
119	    for i, u in enumerate(candidates, start=1):
120	        print(f"[{i}/{len(candidates)}] {u['id']}: {u['listingUrl']}")
121	        body = fetch(u["listingUrl"])
122	        if body:
123	            data = parse(body)
124	            if data:
125	                enriched[u["id"]] = {**data, "fetchedAt": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())}
126	                print(f"  ok: {sorted(data.keys())}")
127	            else:
128	                print("  no fields matched")
129	        ENRICH.write_text(json.dumps(enriched, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
130	        time.sleep(args.sleep)
131	
132	    print(f"done. enrichment.json now has {len(enriched)} entries")
133	
134	
135	if __name__ == "__main__":
136	    main()

Two notes before the critique:

1. The existing snapshots are seeded `u-001..u-028` from the original sample data, NOT keyed on the `u-at-NNN` ids that `build_units_from_at.py` emits. Phase 1.1 as written will produce **zero matches** — see Risks below.
2. Snapshot schema does NOT capture `firstSeen` / `lastSeen` / `listingUrl` / VIN / dealerId-stability. Snapshot-derived daysOnLot can only key on `id`.

---

# Critique of v2 plan

## Phase 1 — Data integrity

### 1.1 Snapshot-derived daysOnLot — **BROKEN AS WRITTEN** [HIGH]
- Three snapshots dated 2025-04-01, 2025-04-15, 2026-05-01 contain `u-001..u-028` (seeded sample). Today's scrape produces `u-at-001..u-at-NNN`. **Zero id overlap → zero coverage.**
- Even if you fix that, only ONE real snapshot (2026-05-01) contains scraped data. "Earliest containing unit_id" = today for every unit → daysOnLot = 0 across the board. Useless until day 4+.
- The id is not a stable identity anyway: `build_units_from_at.py` uses positional `f"u-at-{i:03d}"`. Re-scrape with different result ordering → same listing gets a new id → snapshot diff is meaningless.
- **Fix the fix:** change `build_units_from_at.py` to derive id from `(dealerId, vin || stockNumber || stable-hash(listingUrl))`. THEN snapshot diff works. THEN write `compute_days_on_lot.py`. This is the actual blocker.
- Also: snapshot schema doesn't carry `listingUrl`, only `id`. Either extend the snapshot schema OR key the days-on-lot map by listingUrl-hash.

### 1.2 MSRP source discriminator — **good, simple** [HIGH for design, MEDIUM for wire-up]
- Right call. Replaces the noisy `ask > msrp + 5000` heuristic with ground truth.
- One missing source: `"asking-fallback"` — when both spec lookup AND DEFAULT_MSRP miss, the script currently sets `msrp = L["priceCad"]`. That fallback silently makes the unit look like a non-deal. Mark this case explicitly so UI can hide it from Top Deals entirely.
- Suggest the chip use 3 levels: verified (configurator/spec) / default-table / unverified (asking-fallback). Three is enough; four is over-engineering.

### 1.3 Trim parser hardening — **right but undersized** [HIGH]
- "Ultimate Package" Ioniq5 doesn't exist as a trim — Hyundai Canada calls the top trim **Limited AWD**. The mismatch is probably "Preferred AWD Long Range w/ Ultimate Package" being a real Hyundai US thing or a dealer marketing string. Verify before coding.
- Ioniq9 hierarchy: catalog has Preferred LR RWD/AWD + Performance Calligraphy AWD. There is NO plain "Calligraphy AWD" trim in the catalog. Plan calls out trims that don't exist in `TRIMS["Ioniq9"]`. Either expand the catalog (HIGH-reasoning — touches `constants.ts` + `TRIMS_BY_MODEL`) or fix the script to map dealer marketing strings onto the existing canonical names.
- This task is a recurring whack-a-mole. Pair it with 1.2 — once `msrpSource = "asking-fallback"` is visible in the UI, you SEE which units the parser is failing on. Don't try to fix all trim mismatches blind.

### 1.4 EV9 spec lookup gap — **investigate, don't pre-decide** [HIGH]
- Plan jumps to fix without confirming root cause. Run `jq '.[] | select(.model=="EV9") | .year' data/specs.json` first. If specs are MY2025 only and units are MY2024, the relax-key fix is right. If specs are MY2024 with wrong trim names, different fix.
- 2-min investigation, then 15-min fix. Don't pre-write the fix.

### Phase 1 ordering verdict
Wrong. Correct order:
1. **Stable unit ids first** (id-from-VIN-or-listing-hash in `build_units_from_at.py`) — unblocks 1.1 AND every future snapshot diff
2. **EV9 investigation** (1.4) — 2 min, may unblock half of 1.3
3. **MSRP source discriminator** (1.2) — surfaces 1.3's targets
4. **Re-scrape, observe, then trim parser fixes** (1.3) — guided by the chips
5. **Snapshot-derived daysOnLot** (1.1) — only useful in 4-5 days; defer

---

## Phase 2 — Imperva workaround

### 2.1 Search-results JSON endpoint — **YES, do this first** [HIGH]
- Single-best-bet. AutoTrader's search SPA fetches JSON; the per-listing HTML pages are decoy. If the search JSON includes `daysOnMarket` + dealer phone, you skip enrichment entirely AND get pagination for free.
- 30-min DevTools sniff. If it works, kills 3 blockers and 2 NEXT items at once.

### 2.2 Apify fallback — **defer the decision until 2.1 fails** [HIGH for decision]
- Don't pre-stage the user prompt. If 2.1 works, this never happens.
- If 2.1 fails: Apify is the right answer for a 1-2 week buying window. $10/run, ~3 runs = $30 total. Cheap relative to the price-discovery value.

### 2.3 Imperva-evasion — **kill it** [MEDIUM]
- Cloudscraper / UA rotation against Imperva in 2026 is a losing battle for a personal-use script. Will eat 4-6 hours, fail 60% of the time. Skip entirely. If 2.1 fails, go straight to 2.2.

### Risk I haven't seen flagged
- AutoTrader's search JSON often returns 25-50 results per page. For 5 nameplates × multiple provinces × 15 pages, that's a lot of polite-cadence requests. Imperva may also gate the JSON endpoint. Have a "if even the JSON gates after 50 calls, fall back to Apify" decision tree ready BEFORE you start.

---

## Phase 3 — Decision-support features

### 3.1 Per-unit negotiation card — **already 70% built** [HIGH]
- Read `UnitDrawer.tsx` (run log says it already has caveman negotiation copy with cheapest-comparable + EVAP-aware lines + days-on-lot anchoring). This is a **rewrite/extend**, not a new build. Audit before adding.
- "Used market retention W%" — do you actually have used data for the specific (model, trim, year)? `used-listings.json` exists, but coverage per nameplate is tiny in early data. Render only when ≥3 used comps; otherwise hide.

### 3.2 Email script generator — **already shipped per PROGRESS line `c57f6a4`** [skip]
- "caveman-style negotiation email anchored on days-on-lot, dealer pressure score, and cheapest comparable unit (model+year+trim). Copy-to-clipboard."
- Adding a "customizable greeting via cookie" is polish for a 1-2 week solo-use tool. **Kill this.**

### 3.3 Cross-province delivery breakdown — **good, contained** [HIGH]
- Real value-add. Threading transport into a per-row "effective OTD vs Ontario dealer" delta is exactly the buyer-decision lever for a 1-2 week window.
- One risk: transport bands are flat heuristics. A buyer in ON looking at AB may get $1,200 vs reality of $2,500-$3,500 + 10-day wait. Add an inline tooltip "Estimate; actual can be 50-100% higher" so it doesn't drive a wrong decision.

---

## Phase 4 — Polish + ritual + commit

### 4.1 Heat-pump flag — **ship it, it's THE Ontario decision metric** [MEDIUM execution, HIGH research]
- Demoted to "defer if Phases 1-3 run over." Wrong. For an Ontario buyer, heat pump is THE differentiator on winter range. Higher decision impact than half of Phase 3.
- 5-min-per-nameplate research is overstated. Hyundai/Kia Canada trim sheets are PDFs/configurators; expect 15-20 min per nameplate × 5 = ~90 min. Still a clear win.
- **Promote to Phase 1.5** or run in parallel with Phase 2.

### 4.2 Snapshot ritual — **already operational** [skip / 5 min]
- `npm run snapshot` exists. The "ritual" is just running it during the manual refresh. PROGRESS already documents the workflow. No code work.

### 4.3 Final commits — **mechanical** [MEDIUM]
- Standard. ~3-4 turns including push verification.

---

| Phase | Turns | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (corrected order) | 18-25 | 1 investigation, 4 file edits (`build_units_from_at.py` ×2, `types.ts`, `data.ts`, drawer chip), 1 user pause for trim catalog decisions |
| 2 | 8-15 if 2.1 works; 25-35 if 2.1 fails → Apify | DevTools sniff + 1-2 file rewrites; user-decision pause for Apify spend |
| 3 (pruned) | 12-18 | 3.1 audit + extend (1 file), 3.3 transport delta (2 files); skip 3.2 |
| 4 | 8-12 | Heat-pump research is async user homework; commits ~5 turns |
| **Total** | **45-90** | Wide range driven by 2.1 success/failure |

User-decision pauses required: (a) Apify spend, (b) trim-catalog expansion if Ioniq9 hierarchy is real, (c) heat-pump research delivery format.

---

## Pruning candidates (over-engineered for 1-2 week purchase)

1. **3.2 Email greeting cookie** — solo-use tool, kill it
2. **2.3 Imperva evasion** — sunk-cost trap, kill it
3. **1.1 Snapshot-derived daysOnLot in current form** — only meaningful after 4-5 days of good snapshots; ship the prerequisite (stable ids) and defer the compute script
4. **4.2 "Ritual" formalization** — already documented in NEXT.md, no code
5. **MSRP "configurator" source as a separate enum value (1.2)** — collapse with "spec-lookup". You won't have a separate code path that knows the difference.

---

## Missing items from NEXT.md / BLOCKERS_MEDIUM.md

- **NEXT task A (buyer-province OTD)** — PROGRESS lists a `BuyerProvinceSelector.tsx` and `buyerProvince.ts` already shipped. Confirm A is truly done before plan assumes it. If only partially wired, this is more important than 3.3.
- **NEXT task H (pagination)** — only mentioned obliquely. If 2.1 search-JSON works, pagination comes free. If 2.1 fails, paginating with `build_units_from_at.py` is its own Imperva problem. Make this explicit.
- **NEXT task I (incentives refresh)** — for a 1-2 week buying window with 27 incentives in play (EVAP, Roulez vert, OEM May 2026 subventions per PROGRESS), stale incentives matter. Plan ignores it. **Add as a Phase 1.5 manual ritual** — WebFetch hyundai.ca/promotions + kia.ca/offers, update `incentives.json`. Maybe 3 user pauses.
- **PROGRESS notes EV9 + Ioniq9 specs are `verifyPending`** — overlaps with 1.4. Roll the EV9 fix into a broader "verify EV9 + Ioniq9 specs end-to-end" task.
- **Loyalty / conquest incentive eligibility (Ian-specific)** — does Ian own a current Hyundai/Kia? If yes, loyalty programs unlock thousands. The plan doesn't capture his eligibility flags. This is a single boolean on the buyer-context that filters incentives correctly.

---

## Creative addition — the one I'd actually do [HIGH]

**"Why this car?" per-unit negotiation dossier as a printable PDF/print-stylesheet view.** Single page. URL like `/inventory/u-at-NNN/dossier`. Renders:

- Top: model/trim/year/VIN + dealer + buyer's effective OTD (with EVAP, transport, HST at ON rate)
- Mid: every cheaper or comparable unit nationwide for same trim+year (delta in $ + miles away). Three rows max.
- Bottom: dealer pressure score + same-trim depth at this dealer + days-on-lot + cheapest cross-province comparable
- Footer: pre-written email talking points with the actual numbers inlined

Why this matters for Ian's actual workflow: when he calls a dealer he needs ONE PAGE he can refer to during the conversation, not 8 chrome tabs across 4 routes. The email generator is good but he needs the in-call reference doc. Print stylesheet is ~20 lines of CSS. Use existing data; no new scrapes needed.

This is the "10x value" item — every other Phase 3 feature is a micro-optimization on data Ian still has to re-find before each call.
